newsitem.title: UK: London gold fixes firmer but upside seen limited.
newsitem.headline: London gold fixes firmer but upside seen limited.

text.p: Precious metals prices were mostly higher on Wednesday morning but dealers said they were in range and not going anywhere in a hurry.
"There is not much to go for but the upside resistance (in gold) might be eroding slightly," one dealer said.
Gold was fixed at $328.60 per ounce up from $326.15 on Tuesday afternoon when London closed at $326.10/$326.60.
The gold market has been moving in counter step to the U.S. dollar and the stock and bond markets over the past few days.

A sell-off in the financial markets on Friday gave gold prices a lift which was cut off when they rallied on Monday before turning down again late on Tuesday to give gold a chance to find some buying in Asia.
"We are still basically in a $325-$330 range. You have to play the ranges in a market like this," a dealer said.
One problem for gold was that above the current price producer selling to take advantage of rises would choke off any advances, dealers said.

But any hint of inflation in U.S. retail sales and producer prices for July later on Wednesday could benefit gold. Most impact would be on financial markets but there could be a knock-on effect for gold.
"I am cautiously optimistic for that. It will help that gold is very cheap just now if there is a reaction elsewhere," a dealer said.
Silver is pretty cheap too but has failed to attract sustained interest and there was little business about for it this morning, dealer said.
It was indicated at $4.46/$4.48, up four cents but needing to get above $4.50 to suggest a rally was beginning.
Platinum lease rates were down to around 15 percent from three times that level in June as tightness came out of the market.
Palladium was commanding one-month rates of around 40-60 percent, also well below peak levels, dealers said.
"The worst of their troubles seem to be over but the prices are still very vulnerable to news of deliveries or non-deliveries," a dealer said.
Platinum was indicated at $438.00/$441.00 up $3.50 and palladium was down $0.50 at $226.00/$229.00
